dust_storm.narration.1: Commander, I see a big orange cloud far away. It’s a dust storm, and it will reach us tomorrow.
dust_storm.narration.2: Dust blocks sunlight, so our solar panels will make less power. We have one sol to get ready!
dust_storm.dialogue.1: We can cover the panels, or save energy now.
dust_storm.dialogue.2: Mars storms can last for days. Let’s be ready!
dust_storm.question: How do we get ready?
dust_storm.A.label: Cover the panels (Power −10 now, storm costs only Power −5)
dust_storm.A.after: Smart! The covers keep dust off the panels. We spent power today so we lose less tomorrow.
dust_storm.B.label: Switch off the lab to save energy (Power +5 now, storm costs Power −10, no science)
dust_storm.B.after: We saved some energy by pausing experiments. Science will have to wait for sunnier days.
dust_storm.C.label: Carry on as normal (Science +1, storm costs Power −15)
dust_storm.C.after: We got extra science today, but the storm will cost us more power tomorrow. Planning ahead has a price, and so does skipping it.
dust_storm.classroom: Why spend power before a storm?
